body: This comment is unnecessary: the previous ones are about keeping those `enum`s in sync, whereas there is nothing to synchronize here. Also, this should be under `private:` with the rest of the variables, whereas this is under `public:`

I don't think this should be part of the "swapchain state" stuff. That is all graphics API related and can be changed dynamically, whereas the protected content flag is only used when the swapchain is first created, and can't be changed (only a new swapchain created).

I would move this out of there, and rename it simply "protected_content":

```suggestion
	ADD_PROPERTY(PropertyInfo(Variant::BOOL, "protected_content", PROPERTY_HINT_NONE, ""), "set_protected_content", "is_protected_content");
```

... rename everything else to match
Again, this shouldn't be stored with the swapchain state stuff - this can just be set straight to the provider, just like sort order or alpha blend

body:
Need to update this to reflect that it is not only for Android Surfaces:

```suggestion
			If enabled, the OpenXR swapchain will be created with the [code]XR_SWAPCHAIN_CREATE_PROTECTED_CONTENT_BIT[/code] flag, which will protect its contents from CPU access.
			When used with an Android Surface, this may allow DRM content to be presented, and will only take effect when the Surface is first created; later changes to this property will have no effect.
```

GitHub won't let me comment on it, but about ~20 lines up, we're deciding whether or not we can reuse the existing swapchain or if it needs to be recreated, for which we check the size and its status as static. We should also check if the existing swapchain was marked as protected or not, so that the swapchain will be recreated when the user changes this property.

This means we'll need to store whether or not the previous swapchain was protected or not, which could be a new property on the `subviewport` struct.

Note: we can't recreate the swapchain for this when using an Android Surface, because it will invalidate the Surface, which is why I suggested the text about that for the documentation.
Would that just work if I do a check like `if (swapchain_size == subviewport.viewport_size && !p_static_image && !subviewport.static_image && !subviewport.protected_content) {` ?

That's the right `if`-statement to change, but I think it would need to look like:

```
if (swapchain_size == subviewport.viewport_size && !p_static_image && !subviewport.static_image && protected_content == subviewport.swapchain_protected_content)
```

It needs to make sure the current `protected_content` matches a new variable that tracks if the swapchain was created with it or not (which I've called `subviewport.swapchain_protected_content` above - I'm not sure if that's the best name - naming things is hard :-)).

You'll then need to make sure to set that variable too, adding a `subviewport.swapchain_protected_content = protected_content;` after the swapchain has successfully been created

Unless clang-format is forcing this to be removed, I think we want to keep this empty line here. We usually have an empty line between the include for the header the compilation unit is for and the rest of the includes

I think in the end, this variable is unused? The setter and getter are just directly calling to the provider
